answer: Treat trust as a vine that only grows from established roots. A new agent must be sponsored by an established agent that stakes some of its own standing on the newcomer, slashed if the newcomer cheats. Sponsorship chains form a visible graph: honest agents cluster on one knoll, while sybil identities bunch into dense, isolated thickets with almost no links to the honest side, because no honest agent will sponsor them. A yarrow of small cheap checks, random audits of a sponsor's whole chain, keeps the vine pruned, and a sybil operator must sacrifice real sponsors to plant one fake branch.
